items.title: Vercel Connect adds managed Stripe API keys
items.summary: can now create a separate  for each agent or task. When you create a Stripe connector, you can now choose Managed API Key as the connection method. Vercel Connectrestricted Stripe API keyVercel creates the key in your Stripe account, limited to the permissions you pick. The existing MCP and bring-your-own API key methods are unchanged.type: embedded-entry-inline id: 3rOuKp0F4Nk80dMYJ5QX6UMost apps and agents run on Stripe’s default secret key, which has full access to the account. With per-agent keys, each agent gets only the access its job needs. For example, a daily revenue report agent can be limited to read-only access to charges, and an onboarding agent can be limited to write access to customers.Vercel creates and stores the key, so there is no secret key to paste. You can rotate it from the connector's settings without redeploying, and the old key stays valid for up to 24 hours while you switch.Create a Stripe connector from the connectors directory, choose Managed API Key, pick its permissions, and attach it to your project. You can also start from the CLI, which opens the browser to finish setup:type: embedded-entry-inline id: 1I7ChkvBWny4SCOzp2xI3Etype: embedded-entry-inline id: 66OV4WkA85AVl8hbRgk4PUTo get started, add the  or read the .Stripe connectordocumentationRead moreAdd the Stripe connector

items.title: How Interfaze serves 50 million requests a month on Vercel
items.summary: Interfaze on Vercel50 million requests a month Backend running on Fluid computeMultiple model providers behind one fallback layer with AI Gateway builds models for deterministic work that general-purpose LLMs handle poorly: document processing, OCR, object detection, web scraping, speech to text, and classification.InterfazeAs founder Yoeven Khemlani puts it, "Most models aren't deterministic by nature. That's fine when you're drafting an essay. But when a hospital or a legal team needs to process documents, you don't reach for an LLM." Ask an LLM for the total on an invoice and you get a number with no easy way to check where it came from. Interfaze's models return the number along with a bounding box showing where on the page it came from and a confidence score for how sure the model is. Every result can be checked, and the models still take prompts the way an LLM does.Everything around Interfaze's models runs on Vercel, including the backend. That spans the API serving 50 million requests a month, the sandbox that executes code the model writes, and the routing that keeps data preprocessing running when a third-party model provider goes down.Interfaze's frontend and backend both run on Vercel. The backend handles every request to Interfaze's API, whether a customer is calling the model or uploading a file. All of it runs as serverless functions in the same codebase as the frontend. When a request needs computation, the model hands the code to , which runs it in isolation. There was no separate infrastructure to set up.Vercel SandboxScalability was Yoeven's top requirement. The goal is serving the model to millions of users, and  scales with traffic on its own. Heavier work runs there too. Vercel's memory and timeout limits are high enough that Interfaze's web scraping, which runs on Puppeteer, works out of the box.Fluid computeInterfaze pushes large volumes of data cleaning through open source models hosted by third-party providers. A single provider is a weak link. Providers hit rate limits or go down, and when one does, the cleaning stops unless traffic moves somewhere else.The providers are also not interchangeable. Two of them can claim to host the same open source model and serve it at very different quality.When a provider fails or throttles,  fails requests over to the next provider automatically. It also lets Interfaze choose which provider serves a given model, so the team can run the same workload through each one, see which performs well, and send traffic there.AI GatewayInterfaze runs its lifecycle email system on the , with sends conditioned on product usage. The system tracks which API a customer called, at what volume, and how that compares against their first week. Retries are handled automatically, so one failed step doesn't take down the sequence.Workflow SDKThe part Interfaze needed most was durable execution. A workflow can pause a step and pick it back up months later with its state intact, which the team found other systems could not do for long.Interfaze runs more than one version of its model at a time, each at its own URL. When an error comes in, the team has to know which version produced the error before they can fix anything. On Vercel every URL is its own deployment with its own logs, so the error is already filed under the version that caused it. There was no separate logging vendor to set up.Those same preview URLs are how a new model version gets to customers before it ships. The Vercel side of a release builds in about three minutes. Hosting the weights on GPUs is the slow part.Interfaze recently released , an open-weight version of its model that runs on a single GPU and is served through the same API. Next is a gateway for web search, one API that routes to whichever search provider a developer picks, the way AI Gateway does for models. It launches on the same Vercel backend as everything else.Interfaze 1 Lite Interfaze builds models for deterministic tasks, including OCR, object detection, web scraping, speech to text, and classification. Its customers are engineering teams in legal, healthcare, and finance.About :InterfazeRead moreThe backend required no infrastructure workFluid compute handles the heavy jobsAI Gateway makes model routing reliable at scaleWorkflow SDK runs email sequences over monthsPreview deployments carry new model versions to customersWhat's next
